column1: # Authoring rulings — the facts de.wiktionary does not have.
# `verify.ts` refuses to write a card it cannot verify, and that is the right
# default: a generated sentence with a wrong gender attached is taught, drilled
# and remembered. But the gate had no way to record a fact it *could not look
# up*, so a word de.wiktionary simply has no page for was rejected on every run
# for ever, and whatever a maintainer found out about it lived in a session
# transcript. This file is where that goes, in the manner of
# `corpus/pos-rulings.tsv` and `corpus/gender-audit.tsv`.
# ## What a ruling may do
# Supply a fact **where the dictionary is silent** — no page at all, or a page
# that states no gender. That is the whole surface. Two things it may never do:
#   * **Override a contradiction.** If de.wiktionary attests `das` and the card
#     says `der`, that is still a hard reject and this file cannot reach it.
#     Overriding it is precisely the failure the 2026-08-11 machine-gate decision
#     exists to prevent, and a file that could would reopen it.
#   * **Paper over an unreachable network.** "Could not reach de.wiktionary" is
#     not silence, it is not knowing. Fix the connection and re-run.
# A ruling is therefore a *recorded fact with a citation*, not a permission slip
# — the same thing `gender-audit.tsv` already is. `--report` prints ruled facts
# as their own class so a batch report never lets one read as machine-verified.
# ## Evidence
# A citation somebody else can check: a Wiktionary section the parser could not
# reach, a Wikidata id, a Duden or DWDS headword *consulted* (their text is not
# redistributable — cite, never copy), a course-book page. Never "checked by
# hand": that is the thing this column exists to replace.
# ## Format — five tab-separated columns
#   term      the headword exactly as the card writes it, article included
#   field     gender | plural | pos | ipa
#   value     der/die/das · "die Xs" (with article) · a corpus pos · bare IPA
#   evidence  the citation
#   date      YYYY-MM-DD the ruling was made
# Worked example of the shape (commented out — it is not a real ruling):
#   das Handy
# ## Rot
# `corpus:validate` checks every ruling whose term is in the corpus against the
# card, so a ruling left behind by a merge or an `authoring:recard` fails the
# build rather than quietly disagreeing with the card it was written for. A
# ruling for a term not yet authored is fine and is why the file exists.
# No rulings yet. Add one only when a run has actually reported the dictionary
# silent for that term — never pre-emptively.
term
